<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>

</diagram>

0 5 0

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions

row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>

n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Border cells – non‑zero cells that have a zero neighbour on the outer edge
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,

border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,
    (R = N-2, input(R+1,C,0)).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,
    (C = 1, input(R,C-1,0)).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0,
    (C = M-2, input(R,C+1,0)).

% Outer colour – colour of the outer border (must be unique)
outerColor(O) :- border(R,C,V), O = V.
% uniqueness
:- not exists O1,O2 :- outerColor(O1), outerColor(O2), O1 != O2.

% Interior cells – non‑zero cells whose colour is not the outer colour
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, not outerColor(V).

% Rows and columns that contain interior cells (temporary)
interiorRow(R) :- interior(R,C,V).
interiorCol(C) :- interior(R,C,V).   % placeholder – will be replaced by a proper range

maxColI(Cmax) :- interior(R,Cmax,V), V != 0, not exists C2 : interior(R2,C2,W), C2 > Cmax.

colMinMinus1(Cminus1) :- minColI(C0), Cminus1 = C0 - 1.

interiorCol(C) :- interiorRow(R), input(R,C,_), colMinMinus1(Cminus1), C >= Cminus1, C <= maxColI(Cmax).

colIdx(J,C) :- interiorCol(C), J = #count{C2 : interiorCol(C2), C2 < C }.

% Output cells

% Number of rows and columns
n_rows(N) :- #count{ R : input(R,_,_) }.
row(0..N-1) :- N = #count{ R : input(R,_,_) }.

n_cols(M) :- #count{ C : input(_,C,_) }.
col(0..M-1) :- M = #count{ C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Non-zero cells
nonzero(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0.

% Rows and columns that have at least one non-zero cell
rowsNonZero(R) :- nonzero(R,_,_).
colsNonZero(C) :- nonzero(_,C,_).

% min/max row/col
minRow(N) :- #min{R : rowsNonZero(R)}.
maxRow(N) :- #max{R : rowsNonZero(R)}.
minCol(M) :- #min{C : colsNonZero(C)}.
maxCol(M) :- #max{C : colsNonZero(C)}.

% interior rows and columns
interiorRow(R) :- R > minRow(N), R < maxRow(N).
interiorCol(C) :- C >= minCol(M), C < maxCol(M).

% leaf zero definition
leafZero(ZR,CZ,R,C,V) :- 
    input(ZR,CZ,0), input(R,C,V), V != 0,
    #count{ R1,C1,W : input(R1,C1,W), W != 0, (R1 = ZR+dr, C1 = CZ+dc), (dr,dc) in {(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)} } = 1,
    (R = ZR+dr0, C = CZ+dc0), (dr0,dc0) in {(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)}.

% Outer colour candidate (leaf zero neighbour)
outerCandidate(V) :- leafZero(ZR,CZ,R,C,V), V = V.

% Ensure exactly one distinct outer colour
:- not exists C1, C2 :- outerCandidate(C1), outerCandidate(C2), C1 != C2.

% outer colour variable
outerColour(C) :- outerCandidate(C).

% cellWillBeOuter for interior cells
cellWillBeOuter(R,C) :- interiorRow(R), interiorCol(C), input(R,C,V), V != 0.
cellWillBeOuter(R,C) :- interiorRow(R), interiorCol(C), leafZero(ZR,CZ,R,C,V).

% columnHasOuter: a column is used if there is at least one interior row with cellWillBeOuter
colHasOuter(C) :- interiorRow(R), cellWillBeOuter(R,C), not exists R2 : interiorRow(R2), cellWillBeOuter(R2,C), R2 < R.

% row and column index for output
rowIndex(I,R) :- interiorRow(R), I = #count{ R2 : interiorRow(R2), R2 < R }.

colIndex(J,C) :- interiorCol(C), colHasOuter(C), J = #count{ C2 : interiorCol(C2), colHasOuter(C2), C2 < C }.

% output rules
output(I,J,OC) :- rowIndex(I,R), colIndex(J,C), interiorRow(R), interiorCol(C), colHasOuter(C), cellWillBeOuter(R,C).

output(I,J,0) :- rowIndex(I,R), colIndex(J,C), interiorRow(R), interiorCol(C), colHasOuter(C), not cellWillBeOuter(R,C).

n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

interiorRow(R) :- interior(R,_,_).   % we will define interior later.

interiorCol(C) :- interior(_,C,_).

% Row index mapping for interior rows
rowIndex(I,R) :- interiorRow(R), I = #count{R2 : interiorRow(R2), R2 < R }.

colIndex(J,C) :- interiorCol(C), J = #count{C2 : interiorCol(C2), C2 < C }.

% Compute interior cells (non-zero not border)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, not border(R,C,V).

% Border detection
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, (R > 0, input(R-1,C,0)).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, (R < N-1, input(R+1,C,0)).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, (C > 0, input(R,C-1,0)).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, (C < M-1, input(R,C+1,0)).

% Determine outer color (must be consistent)
outerColor(O) :- border(R,C,V), O = V.

% Uniqueness of outer color
:- not exists O1,O2 :-
    outerColor(O1), outerColor(O2), O1 != O2.

% Mapping rectangle cells
rowIndex(I,R) :- interiorRow(R), I = #count{R2 : interiorRow(R2), R2 < R }.
colIndex(J,C) :- interiorCol(C), J = #count{C2 : interiorCol(C2), C2 < C }.

output(I,J,0) :- rectangle(I,J,R,C), input(R,C,0).

% Exactly one output per cell
1 { output(I,J,Color) : color(C) } 1 :- rectangle(I,J).

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- #count{R : input(R,_,_) }.
n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Border cells (non-zero with zero neighbor)
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, R > 0, input(R-1,C,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, R < N-1, input(R+1,C,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, C > 0, input(R,C-1,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, C < M-1, input(R,C+1,0).

% Outer color (color of border cells)
outerColor(O) :- border(R,C,V), O = V.

% Enforce exactly one outer color
not exists O1,O2 :-
    outerColor(O1), outerColor(O2), O1 != O2.

% Interior cells (non-zero not border)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, not border(R,C,V).

% Row index for interior rows
rowIndex(I,R) :- interior(R,_,_), I = #count{R2 : interior(R2,_,_), R2 < R }.

% Column index for interior columns
colIndex(J,C) :- interior(_,C,_), J = #count{C2 : interior(_,C2,_), C2 < C }.

% Rectangle cell mapping
rectangle(I,J,R,C) :- rowIndex(I,R), colIndex(J,C).

% Output
output(I,J,O) :- rectangle(I,J,R,C), interior(R,C,V), outerColor(O).
output(I,J,0) :- rectangle(I,J,R,C), input(R,C,0).

% Exactly one output per rectangle cell
1 { output(I,J,Col) : color(C) } 1 :- rectangle(I,J,R,C).

% Show output
#show output/3.

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- #count{R : input(R,_,_) }.
n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_,C,_) }.

% Border detection
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, R > 0, input(R-1,C,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, R < N-1, input(R+1,C,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, C > 0, input(R,C-1,0).
border(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, C < M-1, input(R,C+1,0).

% Outer color (must be consistent)
outerColor(O) :- border(R,C,V), O = V.

% Uniqueness of outer color
not exists O1,O2 :-
    outerColor(O1), outerColor(O2), O1 != O2.

% Interior cells (non-zero and not border)
interior(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, not border(R,C,V).

% Row and column indices for interior rows/cols
rowIndex(I,R) :- interior(R,_,_), I = #count{R2 : interior(R2,_,_), R2 < R }.

colIndex(J,C) :- interior(_,C,_), J = #count{C2 : interior(_,C2,_), C2 < C }.

% Rectangle cell
rectangle(I,J,R,C) :- rowIndex(I,R), colIndex(J,C).

% Output: interior cells become outer color, zeros become 0
output(I,J,O) :- rectangle(I,J,R,C), interior(R,C,V), outerColor(O).
output(I,J,0) :- rectangle(I,J,R,C), input(R,C,0).

% Exactly one output per rectangle cell
1 { output(I,J,Col) : color(C) } 1 :- rectangle(I,J,R,C).

% Show output
#show output/3.
